description:
Filed by s527c (2026-10-31).  SILENT WRONG, pre-existing (main ff5f72b5 and the s527c tree agree; perl differs): a `{` that is the FIRST token inside a map / grep / sort block is an ANONYMOUS HASH in perl, whatever follows it; PCL lowers it as a bare block whose list is flattened into the map's result.

perl 5.40.3 vs PCL (base = main + vendor dc242138, tree = s527c):
  my @c = map { { %$_, x => 1 } } ({a=>1}); print scalar(@c), " ", ref($c[0]), "\n";   perl: 1 HASH    PCL: 4 (empty ref)
  my @l = map { { $_, 1 } } 1..2;          print scalar(@l), " ", ref($l[0]), "\n";   perl: 2 HASH    PCL: 4
  (control: map { { name => $_ } } and map { { $_ => 1 } } are right on both: the statement-position look-ahead (§5, word/string then , or =>) and PCL's _block_is_hash_constructor catch those.)
  perl -MO=Deparse: map({+{$_, 1};} (1, 2))

The rule, toke.c yyl_leftcurly, `if (PL_expect == XREF) { block_expectation: ... if (*s == '{') { PL_expect = XTERM; break; }`: the `{` that opens a map/grep/sort block (or a ${ / @{ deref block) is lexed with PL_expect == XREF, and when the next non-space character is another `{` perl sets XTERM, so that inner `{` is a HASHBRACK -- "treat it as a term to make ${{...}}{k} ... dwim".  `%$_, x => 1` -- the copy-with-one-more-key idiom -- is the everyday shape.

Where: a Lexer row for PCL's PPI branch (Lexer.pm _curly: when the parent Block is the block of map/grep/sort or a deref Cast's block and the `{` is its first significant token, it is a Structure::Constructor), then PCL's lowering takes the Constructor (check PExpr::_block_is_hash_constructor / Parser's _bare_block_is_anon_hash read the Constructor, or become inert).  A catalogue section in docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md + a report row in docs/ppi-bug-report.t + t/ppi_bugs_pcl.t when it is fixed (rule 13).  Candidate for s527d / s527e.
subject: map { { %$_, x => 1 } } LIST: a { first inside a map/grep/sort block is an ANON HASH in perl (toke.c XREF block_expectation); PCL flattens it as a block -- silent wrong
